why: A review found the three "My phone was on the counter." lines (10:05, 10:14, 10:56) carried the same weight; earshot heard the first two as the same plain narration. The author asked for each to go deeper: half an excuse, frightened after "Emily?", barely a breath. Three takes per line from tools/vo_tts.py (gemini-3.8-flash-tts, en-gb-training-10), ranked with earshot.

slots.rank_text: a man calmly explaining something to himself in a quiet, steady, reasonable voice
slots.reason: All four rank alike; V09d is the plainest speaking voice ("a man speaking" +3.0, no whisper among its top tags), so the next two can only go deeper from it.

slots.rank_text: a frightened man speaking fast and out of breath, gasping
slots.reason: The clearest fear: AudioSet hears a gasp (0.63); quicker than the old take (1.86 s of speech against 3.46).

slots.rank_text: a man whispering, broken, with almost no voice
slots.reason: All three are whispers; V11b is the one that comes apart: "My phone was..." then a breath of 1.2 s, then "on the counter." Lifted 2.5 dB to the old take's level so it is not lost in the silence.

takes.style: quietly reasonable, half an excuse: explaining the day to himself, holding on to the one small fact that still makes sense; puzzled, not yet afraid
